newsitem.title: USA: NHL ice hockey-BRODEUR GETS 10TH SHUTOUT AS DEVILS BLANK BRUINS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ice hockey-BRODEUR GETS 10TH SHUTOUT AS DEVILS BLANK BRUINS.

text.p: Martin Brodeur stopped 26 shots for his 10th shutout of the season as the New Jersey Devils moved closer to clinching the Eastern Conference with a 2-0 victory over the Boston Bruins Friday.

Bobby Holik and Dave Andreychuk scored 39 seconds apart in the second period to leave the Devils needing just a tie in Sunday's season finale at Philadelphia to clinch first place in the conference for the first time in team history.
A Flyers' tie or loss at Montreal on Saturday also would give New Jersey the East's top seed.
"It's a thing that we have a chance to do that very few do in hockey," said coach Jacques Lemaire about winning the conference.
Jim Carey made 31 saves for the Bruins, who clinched last place overall in the NHL.
"I hope we do well in the draft," said Bruins defenceman Ray Bourque, the long-time team captain.

Brodeur has 22 career shutouts -- sixth on the active list -- and has helped the Devils to 13 blankings this season, sharing one with Mike Dunham. Brodeur is 37-14-13 with an astounding league-best 1.88 goals-against average.
It would be the first time that an NHL goaltender posted a mark better than 1.90 since Bernie Parent did it for Philadelphia with a 1.89 GAA in 1973-74.
Brodeur also became the first goalie with as many as 10 shutouts since Montreal's Ken Dryden in 1976-77.
"It's unbelievable to be compared to Ken Dryden," Brodeur said. "It's an honour to be mentioned with those type players."

In Dallas, the Colorado Avalanche clinched the President's Trophy as the top team in the regular season and secured home-ice advantage throughout the playoffs as Patrick Roy made 38 saves in a 2-1 victory over the Dallas Stars.

Peter Forsberg and Sandis Ozolinsh scored for the defending Stanley Cup champions, who have 107 points with one game remaining. Dallas could have moved past the Avalanche into first place overall with a win.

But Colorado shook off a pair of recent losses to last-place San Jose and ended the Stars' 11-game home unbeaten streak. Jere Lehtinen had the only goal for Dallas, which owns the second seed in the Western Conference after capturing the Central Division title.

In Chicago, Alexei Zhamnov notched his sixth career hat trick and ignited a five-goal second period that boosted the Blackhawks to a playoff-clinching 7-3 victory over the Calgary Flames, who were eliminated from post-season contention.
The Blackhawks secured eighth place in the Western Conference and a first-round meeting with the defending Stanley Cup champion Avalanche.

Chicago has made the playoffs for 28 straight seasons, the longest current streak in the four major North American sports since the Bruins, who had made it for the last 29 years, did not qualify this season.
In Detroit, Wade Redden's goal with 2:32 to play broke a tie as the Ottawa Senators took a major step toward their first-ever playoff berth with a 3-2 win over the Red Wings.
Ron Tugnutt made 27 saves for the Senators, who have 75 points and are one ahead of Tampa Bay for the eighth and final Eastern Conference playoff berth.
On Long Island, Claude Lapointe and Robert Reichel each scored twice as the New York Islanders beat the Hartford Whalers 6-5 and broke a five-game winless streak.
Sami Kapanen tallied twice for Hartford, which fell into 10th place in the Eastern Conference one point behind Tampa Bay and two behind Ottawa.
The Isles were already eliminated from playoff contention.

At Florida, Rob Niedermayer, Ray Sheppard and Kirk Muller scored and John Vanbiesbrouck allowed Mario Lemieux's penalty-shot goal but held on as the Panthers clinched home-ice advantage in the opening round of the playoffs with a 4-2 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins.
The Panthers, in their season finale, clinched fourth place in the Eastern Conference.
In New York, Rob Zamuner scored on a shorthanded breakaway with 19.8 seconds to go in the second period as the Tampa Bay Lightning kept their playoff hopes alive with a 4-2 victory over the Rangers.

Dino Ciccarelli, Daymond Langkow and Chris Gratton also tallied for the Lightning, who jumped over Hartford into ninth place in the Eastern Conference and trail Ottawa by one point in the battle for the final playoff berth.

In Edmonton, Jeremy Roenick set up a pair of first-period tallies and added his 29th goal of the season with 13 seconds left in the second period as the Phoenix Coyotes defeated the Oilers 6-2 in a pivotal game for both teams.
The Coyotes finished with 83 points, tied with Anaheim for fourth place in the Western Conference, but they hold the tiebreaker and will have home advantage against the Ducks.
Edmonton is tied with idle St. Louis for sixth place in the conference.

In San Jose, Paul Kariya scored twice and Teemu Selanne added his 51st goal and an assist as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim completed the most successful season in franchise history with a 4-3 victory over the Sharks.
The Ducks closed the season on a seven-game unbeaten streak (5-0-2). The Ducks had never qualified for the post-season.
